comment: Annex D.1 lists two illustrative implementations under Lifelong Health Record: HAPI FHIR Server, "an open-source, FHIR-conformant server widely used as a technical foundation for health record repositories", and EHRbase, "an open-source, openEHR-conformant clinical data repository that stores and queries health data against openEHR archetypes and templates". The annex therefore treats both a FHIR server and an openEHR repository as valid technical foundations for the LHR. Figures 3.2 and 3.5, however, both annotate the Lifelong Health Record element as a "FHIR-based store", and design principle II at page 32 lines 233–234 names FHIR-based approaches as the direction of travel. The illustrative annex, the figures and the design principle give countries different answers to the same question. Taken with Appendix C page 175 functional requirement 2, which makes openEHR archetypes a required LIMR formalism, the guidance accepts openEHR in three places and omits it from the three places a ministry or a procurement team will actually read.

public.suggestedRevision: Align them. If Annex D.1 is correct that both a FHIR server and an openEHR clinical data repository are valid foundations for the Lifelong Health Record — and the Ministry’s national experience is that both are — then the annotation in Figures 3.2 and 3.5 should read "openEHR / FHIR" rather than "FHIR-based store", and principle II should name both. These are small changes and they remove an inconsistency that any reader comparing the figures with the annex will find immediately.
